item.vignette: A 4-month-old boy has severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, muscular hypotonia, and recurrent lactic acidosis. Respiratory-chain complex activities in skeletal muscle are preserved, but isolated muscle mitochondria have markedly reduced oxidative ATP synthesis. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC25A3.
item.lead_in: Which mitochondrial transport process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Import of inorganic phosphate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
options.B: Exchange of cytosolic ADP for mitochondrial ATP through adenine nucleotide translocase
options.C: Import of pyruvate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
options.D: Export of mitochondrial aspartate in exchange for cytosolic glutamate plus a proton
options.E: Exchange of acylcarnitine for free carnitine across the inner mitochondrial membrane

item.tested_construct: SLC25A3 is the mitochondrial phosphate carrier that imports inorganic phosphate into the matrix for oxidative phosphorylation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: SLC25A3 encodes the mitochondrial phosphate carrier. Inorganic phosphate must enter the mitochondrial matrix so ATP synthase can phosphorylate ADP. Loss of SLC25A3 therefore impairs oxidative ATP synthesis even when the respiratory-chain complexes themselves remain intact.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. SLC25A3 transports inorganic phosphate into the mitochondrial matrix, supplying a substrate required for ATP synthesis.
distractor_explanations.B: Adenine nucleotide translocase exchanges matrix ATP for cytosolic ADP, but it is encoded by a different SLC25 family member and does not transport phosphate.
distractor_explanations.C: The mitochondrial pyruvate carrier imports pyruvate for oxidation; its loss does not directly remove the phosphate substrate required by ATP synthase.
distractor_explanations.D: Citrin/AGC2 mediates aspartate-glutamate exchange and is mechanistically distinct from the phosphate carrier.
distractor_explanations.E: The carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase exchanges acylcarnitine and carnitine during long-chain fatty-acid oxidation; it does not supply phosphate for ATP synthesis.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize SLC25A3 deficiency as impaired mitochondrial inorganic-phosphate import, limiting oxidative ATP synthesis despite preserved respiratory-chain complex activities.

item.vignette: A 10-month-old girl has congenital microcephaly, developmental delay, and recurrent intractable seizures. Cultured fibroblasts are unusually sensitive to ionizing radiation and repair induced DNA strand breaks slowly. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in PNKP.
item.lead_in: Which DNA-end processing activity is most directly impaired?

options.A: Removal of 8-oxoguanine from damaged DNA by a base-excision glycosylase
options.B: Phosphorylation of DNA 5-prime hydroxyl ends and dephosphorylation of DNA 3-prime phosphate ends
options.C: Poly-ADP-ribosylation at strand breaks to recruit repair proteins
options.D: Nuclease-mediated resection of double-strand break ends to create 3-prime single-stranded overhangs
options.E: ATP-dependent ligation of compatible double-strand break ends by DNA ligase IV

item.tested_construct: PNKP is a bifunctional DNA-end processing enzyme with 5-prime kinase and 3-prime phosphatase activities
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: PNKP processes damaged DNA termini so they can be repaired. Its 5-prime kinase activity phosphorylates 5-prime hydroxyl ends, and its 3-prime phosphatase activity removes obstructive 3-prime phosphates, restoring termini compatible with downstream polymerase and ligase reactions. Loss of PNKP impairs DNA strand-break repair and causes microcephaly with early-onset seizures.

distractor_explanations.A: OGG1 removes oxidized guanine bases during base-excision repair; it does not perform the dual DNA-end processing reaction of PNKP.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. PNKP has DNA 5-prime kinase and DNA 3-prime phosphatase activities that restore repair-compatible strand-break termini.
distractor_explanations.C: PARP1 senses many single-strand breaks and catalyzes poly-ADP-ribosylation, but it does not provide the PNKP end-cleaning activities.
distractor_explanations.D: MRE11-CtIP-dependent resection contributes to homologous recombination at double-strand breaks; it is not the defining PNKP reaction.
distractor_explanations.E: DNA ligase IV seals compatible ends during nonhomologous end joining; PNKP acts upstream by converting damaged termini into ligatable 5-prime phosphate and 3-prime hydroxyl ends.

explanation.educational_objective: Link PNKP-associated microcephaly and seizures to defective DNA strand-break end processing caused by loss of 5-prime kinase and 3-prime phosphatase activities.

item.vignette: A 17-year-old boy develops juvenile parkinsonism, pyramidal signs, and progressive cognitive decline. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in ATP13A2. Patient fibroblasts accumulate spermine within dysfunctional lysosomes and are unusually susceptible to lysosomal rupture under polyamine stress.
item.lead_in: Which transport process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Export of cystine from lysosomes into the cytosol by cystinosin
options.B: Egress of unesterified cholesterol from late endosomes and lysosomes through NPC1/NPC2
options.C: ATP-dependent export of polyamines, especially spermine, from the lysosomal lumen to the cytosol
options.D: ATP-dependent proton transport into lysosomes by the vacuolar proton pump
options.E: Release of lysosomal calcium through the mucolipin-1 channel

item.tested_construct: ATP13A2 is a lysosomal polyamine exporter with high affinity for spermine
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: ATP13A2 is a lysosomal P5B-type ATPase that exports polyamines from the lysosomal lumen toward the cytosol, with particularly high affinity for spermine. Loss of this transport function promotes lysosomal polyamine accumulation, lysosomal dysfunction, and vulnerability to membrane rupture, providing a mechanistic link to ATP13A2-associated juvenile parkinsonism.

distractor_explanations.A: Cystinosin exports cystine from lysosomes and is defective in cystinosis; it is not the ATP13A2 substrate pathway.
distractor_explanations.B: NPC1/NPC2 mediate lysosomal cholesterol egress; their loss causes Niemann-Pick type C rather than a primary polyamine-export defect.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. ATP13A2 exports lysosomal polyamines and shows particularly high affinity for spermine.
distractor_explanations.D: V-ATPase acidifies lysosomes by pumping protons inward; ATP13A2 instead transports polyamines.
distractor_explanations.E: MCOLN1/TRPML1 mediates lysosomal calcium release and is defective in mucolipidosis IV; it does not account for spermine accumulation in ATP13A2 deficiency.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize ATP13A2-associated neurodegeneration as a lysosomal transport disorder in which defective polyamine, especially spermine, export disrupts lysosomal homeostasis.

item.vignette: An 8-year-old boy has early-onset spastic paraplegia, developmental delay, dysarthria, and a thin corpus callosum. Brain proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy shows an unusually large lipid signal, and imaging studies suggest widespread neuronal lipid-droplet accumulation. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in DDHD2.
item.lead_in: Which cellular metabolic defect most directly explains the lipid accumulation?

options.A: Failure of lysosomal cholesteryl-ester and triglyceride hydrolysis by lysosomal acid lipase
options.B: Failure of peroxisomal import and beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids
options.C: Failure of lysosomal sphingomyelin degradation by acid sphingomyelinase
options.D: Reduced intracellular triglyceride hydrolysis in the central nervous system, causing ectopic lipid-droplet accumulation
options.E: Failure of mitochondrial cardiolipin remodeling by tafazzin

item.tested_construct: DDHD2 functions as a major intracellular triglyceride hydrolase in the central nervous system; loss promotes neuronal lipid-droplet accumulation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: DDHD2 is a serine hydrolase with important neutral-lipid lipase activity in the central nervous system. DDHD2 loss markedly reduces intracellular triglyceride hydrolysis and produces ectopic lipid-droplet accumulation in neurons, a characteristic biochemical feature of SPG54.

distractor_explanations.A: Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency causes cholesteryl-ester and triglyceride accumulation in lysosomes, especially in liver and macrophages; it is not the DDHD2-dependent neuronal neutral-lipid defect.
distractor_explanations.B: Peroxisomal very-long-chain fatty-acid oxidation defects cause characteristic VLCFA accumulation but do not explain the DDHD2-associated neuronal lipid-droplet phenotype.
distractor_explanations.C: Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency causes sphingomyelin accumulation in lysosomes and is mechanistically distinct from neutral triglyceride hydrolysis by DDHD2.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. DDHD2 is a major CNS triglyceride hydrolase, and loss of its activity causes ectopic lipid-droplet accumulation.
distractor_explanations.E: TAFAZZIN remodels cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane; its loss causes Barth syndrome rather than the DDHD2/SPG54 lipid-droplet phenotype.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize DDHD2-associated SPG54 as a neuronal lipid-metabolism disorder in which reduced intracellular triglyceride hydrolysis causes ectopic lipid-droplet accumulation.

item.vignette: A 2-year-old girl has developmental regression, hypotonia, lactic acidosis, and symmetric basal-ganglia lesions consistent with Leigh syndrome. Muscle studies show combined oxidative-phosphorylation deficiency. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in MTFMT, and patient fibroblasts have markedly reduced mitochondrial protein synthesis.
item.lead_in: Which reaction involving mitochondrial methionyl-tRNA is most directly impaired?

options.A: Addition of the terminal CCA sequence to mitochondrial transfer RNAs
options.B: Charging of mitochondrial tRNA-Met with methionine by mitochondrial methionyl-tRNA synthetase
options.C: Pseudouridylation of mitochondrial ribosomal and transfer RNAs
options.D: Taurine-containing wobble-base modification of selected mitochondrial transfer RNAs
options.E: Formylation of mitochondrial methionyl-tRNA to generate N-formylmethionyl-tRNA used for translation initiation

item.tested_construct: MTFMT formylates mitochondrial Met-tRNA to generate fMet-tRNA required for efficient mitochondrial translation initiation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among clinically plausible foundational-science alternatives; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Human mitochondria use a single tRNA-Met pool for both initiation and elongation. MTFMT formylates a portion of charged mitochondrial Met-tRNA to produce N-formylmethionyl-tRNA, the initiator species used for efficient mitochondrial translation initiation. Loss of MTFMT reduces fMet-tRNA and impairs mitochondrial protein synthesis.

distractor_explanations.A: CCA addition is required for aminoacylation of tRNAs but is mediated by a distinct tRNA nucleotidyltransferase.
distractor_explanations.B: MARS2 charges mitochondrial tRNA-Met with methionine; MTFMT acts after aminoacylation by adding a formyl group.
distractor_explanations.C: Pseudouridylation is performed by RNA-modifying enzymes and is not the MTFMT-dependent modification.
distractor_explanations.D: Taurine-containing wobble modifications affect decoding by selected mitochondrial tRNAs and are mechanistically distinct from initiator Met-tRNA formylation.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. MTFMT generates N-formylmethionyl-tRNA from mitochondrial Met-tRNA, enabling efficient initiation of mitochondrial translation.

explanation.educational_objective: Link MTFMT-associated Leigh syndrome to defective formylation of mitochondrial methionyl-tRNA and impaired mitochondrial translation initiation.
